title: He conjured up the scene before them.
html_source:
In Oxen of the Sun, Joyce has another objective in addition to just parodying Horace Walpole; he also adds commentary on the state of affairs in Ireland. He appoints Buck Mulligan spokesman, and has him relate, in his typically caustic and flippant manner, a tale that “began to freeze them with horror.” As R. M. Adams reminds us, “Ireland is a land of walking ghosts and barely vitalized corpses,” and Mulligan presents his listeners, in an ante room in the National Maternity Hospital, a highly unique staging for a mostly rowdy conversation among mostly young men, only some of whom, as medical students and residents, have a clear reason for being there. “The secret panel beside the chimney slid back and in the recess appeared… Haines!”

This highly symbolic character, and roommate to Mulligan and Stephen, is used at times in Ulysses to caricaturize the upper-crust, superior, dominating English who have “usurped” Ireland for their own exploitation. That, of the three roommates in the Martello tower, he, the Englishman, was the only one to have studied the “Erse” (Gaelic) language indicts the Irish as having abandoned its culture, and Haines is all too willing to laud it over the others for his eminence. Haines claims responsibility for the Childs murder case, in which the victim and his family, despite the victim’s brother being accused of the crime, were respectable, upper-middle class, the father a former service provider to the Viceroy, the victim a literary and highly respected Church of Ireland clergyman, whose open book on the history of the Bible was splattered with blood at the scene, the accused a successful accountant.

Could Joyce be inferring that Haines, as surrogate for the English, had destroyed this respectable, genteel part of Ireland, and left it with the crudeness and boorishness such as was displayed by this band of young men that evening at the hospital, educated, and seemingly accomplished as they were? The guilt-ridden ghost Haines exclaims, “My hell, and Ireland’s, is in this life. It is what I tried to obliterate my crime. Distractions, rookshooting…, laudanum…, In vain! His [Ireland’s?] spectre stalks me. Dope is my only hope… Ah! Destruction! The black panther!”
